nodes.summary: Write $\mathrm{val}(l)$ for the value of a bit list $l$ read as a binary number least significant bit first, and for a bit $b$ write $[b]$ for $1$ if $b$ is true and $0$ if $b$ is false. For every bit $b$ and every bit list $l$, the list with first entry $b$ followed by $l$ has value $[b] + 2 \cdot \mathrm{val}(l)$.
nodes.title: Value of a bit list with a leading bit

nodes.summary: Write $\mathrm{val}(l)$ for the value of a bit list $l$ read as a binary number least significant bit first. Let $f$ assign to each bit a list of exactly two bits. Then for every bit list $b_0, b_1, \dots, b_{m-1}$, the concatenation $f(b_0) f(b_1) \cdots f(b_{m-1})$ has value $\sum_{q < m} 4^q \, \mathrm{val}(f(b_q))$.
nodes.title: Value of a list of two-bit digits

nodes.summary: For a bit $t$, the block is the four-bit list $(\mathrm{true}, t, \mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false})$.
nodes.title: Output block of a vertex-number digit

nodes.summary: For every bit list $u = (u_1, \dots, u_k)$, the self-delimiting form of $u$ followed by the bit true is $(\mathrm{true}, u_1, \mathrm{true}, u_2, \dots, \mathrm{true}, u_k, \mathrm{true}, \mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false})$.
nodes.title: Delimiting a bit list that ends in true

nodes.summary: For $q \in \mathbb{N}$ and a bit $b$: if $b$ is true, the block is $q$ copies of $(\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false})$ followed by $(\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false})$; if $b$ is false, it is the one-bit list $(\mathrm{false})$.
nodes.title: Output block of an edge number

nodes.summary: Write $E(q, b)$ for the output block of the edge number of pair $q$ with bit $b$. For a bit list $(b_{m-1}, \dots, b_1, b_0)$, listing the bit of the last pair first, the output is the concatenation $E(0, b_0) \, E(1, b_1) \cdots E(m-1, b_{m-1})$.
nodes.title: Output of all edge numbers

nodes.summary: Read a bit list $l$ as a binary number, least significant bit first. The binary code of its value (least significant bit first, with no trailing false bits) is $l$ with all of its trailing false bits removed.
nodes.title: Binary code of the value of a bit list

nodes.summary: For every bit list $l$ whose last entry is not false (the empty list included), the binary code, least significant bit first, of the value of $l$ read least significant bit first is $l$ itself.
nodes.title: A bit list without trailing false is the binary code of its value

nodes.summary: On the result of a pop, which is either a symbol or nothing (when the stack was empty), the test returns true exactly when the result is the input-bit symbol $\mathrm{bit}(\mathrm{true})$, and false otherwise.
nodes.title: Test for the input bit true (SUBSET-SUM reduction machine)

nodes.summary: On the result of a pop, which is either a symbol or nothing (when the stack was empty), the test returns true exactly when the result is the value symbol $\mathrm{val}(\mathrm{true})$, which this machine uses for a pair bit or vertex mark that is true, and false otherwise.
nodes.title: Test for the value symbol true (SUBSET-SUM reduction machine)

nodes.summary: The machine has fifteen stacks: the input $X$ and the output $O$; $A$, which holds the cover size $k$, and $H$, used to halve it; $N$, which holds the number $n$ of vertices, and $M$, the pair count; $C$, which counts the pair bits; the scratch stacks $S_1$ and $S_2$; $Y$ and $Z$, which hold the pair bits; $T$, which holds the target's bits; and $L$, $R$ and $R_t$, which hold the vertex marks.
nodes.title: Stacks of the SUBSET-SUM reduction machine

nodes.summary: The control labels of the subset-sum emitter machine are: $\mathrm{rdK}$, $\mathrm{rdN}$ and $\mathrm{mv}$ (parsing the two unary numbers $k$ and $n$ that open the input, and moving the pair bits); $\mathrm{tri}$, $\mathrm{triC}$, $\mathrm{triC2}$, $\mathrm{cmp}$ and, for every ordering $o$, the labels $\mathrm{rc}(o)$ and $\mathrm{rcB}(o)$ (counting the pairs and comparing that count with the number of pair bits);…
nodes.title: Labels of the subset-sum emitter

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $v$, the list of $n$ bits whose entries, from first to last, record for $i = n-1, n-2, \dots, 0$ whether $i = v$.
nodes.title: Vertex marks for a vertex

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the triangular number $T(n)$ is the sum $0 + 1 + \cdots + (n - 1)$ of the natural numbers below $n$. It is defined by recursion: $T(0) = 0$ and $T(i + 1) = T(i) + i$.
nodes.title: Triangular numbers

nodes.summary: The unit symbol of the counters of the VERTEX-COVER to SUBSET-SUM machine is the token symbol $\mathrm{cl}$; a counter with value $n$ holds exactly $n$ copies of it.
nodes.title: Counter unit of the subset-sum emitter

nodes.summary: In the VERTEX-COVER to SUBSET-SUM machine the output stack $\mathsf{O}$ holds Booleans, and every other stack holds token symbols.
nodes.title: Stack alphabets of the subset-sum emitter

nodes.summary: The partial map from token symbols to bits that sends the symbol $\mathrm{val}(b)$ to $b$ and gives no value on every other symbol.
nodes.title: Reading a pair bit or vertex mark

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a function from the natural numbers to the booleans, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $W$ be the pair walk. For every $i \le n$, let $L$ be the list $f(i - 1), \dots, f(1), f(0)$ (empty when $i = 0$) and $R$ the list $f(i), f(i + 1), \dots, f(n - 1)$ (empty when $i = n$). Then $W(L, R)$ is obtained as follows: list the pairs $(a, j)$ of natural numbers with $a < i$ and $a < j < n$, with $a$ ascending…
nodes.title: The pair walk lists the vertex pairs in reverse

nodes.summary: For lists $L$ and $R$ of booleans, the pair walk $W(L, R)$ is the list of pairs of booleans defined by recursion on $L$. If $L$ is empty, then $W(L, R)$ is empty. If $L$ has first entry $a$ and remaining entries $L'$, then $W(L, R)$ consists of the pairs $(a, r)$ for the entries $r$ of $R$ in order, followed by $W(L', R')$, where $R'$ is the list $R$ with $a$ put in front.
nodes.title: The pair walk over lists of marks

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $v$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be the number of vertex pairs in encoding order for $n$, and let $b$ be a list of $m$ pair bits. Let $L$ be the list of vertex marks for $v$ among $n$, let $(x_0, y_0), \dots, (x_{k-1}, y_{k-1})$ be the pair walk $W(L, [\,])$, and let $c_0, \dots, c_{m-1}$ be the list $b$ reversed. nodes.title: Touch bits from the pair walk of a vertex
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
